Which side of the boundary is the point on?

The key idea SVM is a supervised learning method. This lab uses its SVC classifier.
How do SVM and KNN differ?

KNN uses the votes of the nearest neighbours of a new point. SVM first learns a boundary between classes. C in SVM weights the penalty for violations; it is not the number of neighbours k in KNN. The SVM family also includes SVR for regression.

Experiment

What is a kernel?

A kernel computes the dot product of two points in a transformed space without explicitly constructing its coordinates. This plot uses a separate model trained on two Iris features: 120 training flowers, three classes. Scaling is fitted on train only. The displayed score is training accuracy. The model on pages 4–6 uses all four features.

Why three colors?

The three colors represent the three Iris species. SVM compares three pairs and selects the class with the most votes. The 3 in Polynomial is the polynomial degree, not the class count.

An important step

StandardScaler scales each feature using its mean and standard deviation. It is fitted only on training data. The Pipeline applies the same transformation to a new flower.

Metrics in plain language

Precision: what proportion of predictions for this class is correct?

Recall: what proportion of the actual samples in this class did we find?

F1: the harmonic mean of precision and recall.

Interpreting the result

This accuracy applies only to these 30 flowers. A different split or new data may produce a different result. Evaluate errors and per-class metrics as well as accuracy.

If your teacher asks how to find the best C

Pass lists of C and gamma values to GridSearchCV. It compares mean accuracy over five folds within the training set. Get the parameters with search.best_params_and the fitted model with search.best_estimator_ . The test set is not used for parameter selection.

METHOD AND SOURCES

Where do the results come from?

Pages 1–2 use a synthetic two-class example to explain a pairwise boundary. Page 3 uses three Iris classes, two selected features and 120 training flowers. Each combination is fitted with scikit-learn SVC; the browser computes pairwise voting from the saved support vectors.

Pages 4–6: load_iris(), 150 samples, 4 features. train_test_split(test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=y). Pipeline: StandardScaler → SVC. Baseline model: RBF, C=1, gamma='scale'.

GridSearchCV: C=[0.1,1,10,100], gamma=[0.01,0.1,1,10], StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=42), accuracy. Tied maximum CV scores select the first pair in search order. Best means best for this grid and CV setup only.

The browser computes Iris predictions from the three pairwise decisions of the fitted model. Tied votes select the first class using the default SVC rule. Probabilities are not displayed.
